definitions.gloss: tactile paving; Braille block; textured ground surface indicator
definitions.explanation: Yellow raised blocks installed on sidewalks, train platforms, and public spaces to guide visually impaired people. Invented in Japan in 1965 and now used worldwide.

examples.japanese: {点字|てんじ}ブロックの{上|うえ}に{荷物|にもつ}を{置|お}かないでください。
examples.english: Please do not place luggage on the tactile paving.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}のホームには{点字|てんじ}ブロックが{設置|せっち}されている。
examples.english: Tactile blocks are installed on the station platform.

examples.japanese: {点字|てんじ}ブロックは{目|め}の{不自由|ふじゆう}な{方|かた}が{安全|あんぜん}に{歩|ある}けるように{作|つく}られたものだ。
examples.english: Tactile blocks were created so that visually impaired people can walk safely.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Invented by Seiichi Miyake in Okayama, Japan in 1965. The yellow color was chosen for high visibility. There are two types: dots ({点状|てんじょう}) for warnings (such as platform edges) and lines ({線状|せんじょう}) for directional guidance. In Japan, it is considered poor manners to stand on or block tactile paving.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {点字|てんじ}ブロックを{設置|せっち}する (to install tactile paving)
- {点字|てんじ}ブロックの{上|うえ}に{立|た}つ (to stand on tactile paving)
- {点字|てんじ}ブロックに{沿|そ}って{歩|ある}く (to walk along tactile paving)
